questions.text: Talk about your favourite subject at school.
questions.sampleAnswer: My favourite subject at school was biology. I was lucky to have a teacher who made every lesson feel like an experiment rather than a lecture. For example, instead of just reading about plants, we grew our own seeds and measured them every week. I enjoyed it because it explained how the world around me actually works, and it is still the reason I find science documentaries so interesting today.

questions.text: Describe a skill you learned outside of a classroom.
questions.sampleAnswer: One skill I learned outside the classroom is cooking. I started when I moved away from home and realised I could not live on fast food forever. I mostly learned by watching videos and making a lot of mistakes. Over time, it has helped me save money and eat more healthily, and it has also become a way to relax after a long day.

questions.text: Some people believe exams are the best way to measure what students have learned. Explain whether you agree or disagree.
questions.sampleAnswer: I partly disagree that exams are the best way to measure learning. Exams are efficient and fair in the sense that everyone answers the same questions under the same conditions. However, they mostly reward memorisation and the ability to perform under pressure. For instance, a student might understand a topic deeply but freeze during a timed test. In my view, a combination of projects, presentations and shorter assessments gives a far more accurate picture of what someone has actually learned.

Talk about an app you use every day.
cues: What do you use it for?
questions.sampleAnswer: An app I use every day is a calendar app on my phone. I use it to plan my classes, my work shifts and even my practice time for English. It sends me reminders, so I rarely forget anything important. I would definitely recommend it, especially to busy people, because it keeps everything organised in one place.

questions.text: Describe how technology has changed the way people communicate.
questions.sampleAnswer: Technology has completely changed how people communicate. In the past, people wrote letters or made expensive phone calls, so conversations were less frequent but often more meaningful. Today, we can send instant messages or make free video calls to anyone in the world. Overall, I think the change is positive because it keeps families connected across long distances, although it also means we sometimes pay more attention to our screens than to the people sitting next to us.

questions.text: What do you do to protect the environment?
questions.sampleAnswer: I try to protect the environment with a few small habits. First, I carry a reusable water bottle, so I almost never buy plastic bottles. Second, I switch off lights and chargers when I leave a room. These things might seem small, but if millions of people do them, they make a real difference to the amount of waste and energy we use.

questions.text: Describe an environmental problem in your city or country.
Is it the responsibility of individuals or governments to tackle climate change? Explain your answer.
questions.sampleAnswer: I believe tackling climate change is a shared responsibility, but governments must lead. Individuals can certainly make a difference by using public transport or reducing waste. However, the biggest sources of emissions, such as power plants and heavy industry, can only be changed through policy and investment. For example, when a government funds renewable energy, it affects millions of people at once. So individuals should do their part, but without strong government action, personal efforts will never be enough.

questions.text: Describe your typical morning routine.
cues: What time do you wake up?
questions.sampleAnswer: On weekdays I usually wake up at around half past six. The first thing I do is drink a glass of water and open the curtains to let some light in. Then I take a quick shower, get dressed and have a simple breakfast, normally toast and coffee. Before I leave, I spend ten minutes checking my schedule so that I know exactly what the day looks like.

Talk about a place you would like to visit.
cues: Why do you want to go?
questions.sampleAnswer: One place I would really like to visit is Japan, especially the city of Kyoto. I would love to walk around the old temples, try traditional food and see the cherry blossoms in spring. I want to go there because Japanese culture combines very old traditions with modern technology, and I think experiencing that in person would be fascinating.

Describe a job you would like to have in the future.
What qualities make someone a good colleague?
questions.sampleAnswer: In my opinion, a good colleague needs three main qualities. The first is reliability, because a team only works when people do what they promise. The second is good communication; a colleague who explains problems early saves everyone a lot of time. Finally, a good colleague is willing to help. For example, in my last job, a coworker stayed late to help me finish a report, and that made me want to support her in the same way.

questions.text: Describe a family member you admire.
Talk about a family tradition that is important to you.
questions.sampleAnswer: A family tradition that is very important to me is our big dinner at the end of every year. My grandparents, aunts, uncles and cousins all come together, and everyone brings a dish they have cooked. After dinner, we share the best and worst moments of our year. It is important to me because we live in different cities, so this is the one evening when the whole family is together and we really listen to each other.

questions.text: How have family roles changed compared with your grandparents' generation?

Describe a time when you had to make a difficult decision.
cues: Are you happy with your choice?
questions.sampleAnswer: A difficult decision I had to make was whether to accept a job in another city. On one hand, it was a great opportunity with a better salary. On the other hand, it meant leaving my family and friends. After thinking about it for a week and talking to people I trust, I decided to accept. Looking back, I am happy with my choice because I have grown a lot, and I have learned how to be more independent.

What do you do to stay healthy?
questions.sampleAnswer: To stay healthy, I focus on three things. First, I try to walk or cycle for at least thirty minutes every day. Second, I cook at home most of the time, so I eat more vegetables and less sugar. Finally, I try to sleep seven or eight hours a night, because when I am tired I make worse choices about food and exercise.

Why are you learning English, and how will it help your future?
questions.sampleAnswer: I am learning English mainly because I want to study for a master's degree abroad. Most of the best programmes in my field are taught in English, so a strong score on the Duolingo English Test is my first step. I study every day by watching videos, reading articles and practising speaking out loud. In the future, I believe good English will open doors to international jobs and help me work with people from many different countries.
